citation: Jäkel, Heinlein, Morgenstern, Kim & Klemt-Albert (2025), ITcon 30:603-630
information_architecture: IFC -> IFCtoLBD -> RDF/BOT/PROPS -> BROT/BRCOMP reclassification -> SODIA ontology instances -> Stardog graph DB -> SPARQL; alt path: IFC+TTL+SODIA -> ICDD container (ISO 21597) -> linksets -> SPARQL
identity_mechanism: Converter-generated RDF-instance URI is primary key; actual IFC GlobalId retained only as a property value (props:globalIdIfcRoot_attribute_simple). ICDD-linkset variant explicitly binds via ls:StringBasedIdentifier + GUID for the IFC side vs ls:URIBasedIdentifier for the TTL side.
validation_method: 12 executed SPARQL queries (10 data-integrated + 2 ICDD) against manually-created RDF triples; narrated results, no pre-registered expected-answer set, no denominators
already_established: Ontology + SPARQL linking of NDE diagnostic results to BIM components; 13-CQ-driven query validation; one domain-rule negative test (access-count violation); explicit dual identifier scheme (converter URI vs actual IFC GUID) in ICDD linksets; one inverse-relationship consistency check
remaining_gap: No maintenance/action record concept at all; no identity-verification/duplicate-GUID handling; no provenance of the IFC->RDF transformation itself; no validity scope; no deliberate identity/link-integrity negative tests (only one domain business-rule test); no pre-registered expected-answer protocol
impact_on_paper2: Cannot claim novelty for ontology+SPARQL linking of diagnostic evidence to BIM components or for CQ-driven validation in general; must differentiate via accountable Inspection_Record+Action_Status
column25: identity verification against actual exported IFC

citation: Hagedorn, Liu, König, Hajdin, Blumenfeld, Stöckner, Billmaier, Grossauer & Gavin (2023), JCCE 37(1):04022041
information_architecture: IFC -> IFCtoLBD (RDF) + existing relational AMS DB -> R2RML mapping -> ICDD information container (Ontology/Payload-documents/Payload-triples) -> BOT/BROT/EUROTL/PROV/ASBING ontologies -> SPARQL/SHACL via 5-layer web platform
identity_mechanism: URI-based (BOT/BROT instance URIs from IFCtoLBD, e.g. elements:abutmentEast); raw IFC GlobalId as a distinct retained property is NOT discussed anywhere in the paper
validation_method: Two illustrative use-case demonstrations (visual bridge inspection; pavement maintenance plan) with SPARQL-query screenshots; no CQs listed up front, no pre-registered expected answers, no pass/fail count
already_established: Real, ISO-19650/ISO-21597-grounded whole-container version continuity (status codes work-in-progress/shared/published/archived + previous-version predicate); genuine W3C PROV usage for actor/activity provenance on an inspection instance (prov:Activity, prov:wasAssociatedWith); concrete BIM-component -> condition-record -> maintenance-plan chain via R2RML on a real relational AMS database
remaining_gap: No per-component/per-GUID identity verification or duplicate/version-across-revision handling (only whole-container versioning); maintenance linkage stops at a planned work item, never reaches an executed/status-tracked/closable action; no validity-scope concept; no CQ-driven pre-registered validation; no deliberate negative/invalid-link tests; no reverse query demonstrated; authors explicitly flag live sensor connection as unaddressed future work
impact_on_paper2: Cannot claim to be first to use PROV for actor provenance or to model information-package version continuity; must differentiate via component-level (GUID-bound
column25: export-verified) identity governance and a closed accountable Action_Status

citation: Yin, Liu, Chen, Wang & Al-Hussein (2020), Tunnelling and Underground Space Technology 97:103252
information_architecture: Monitoring sensors (fire/video/environmental/security/equipment) -> gateway/middleware -> SQL relational O&M database <- BIM (Revit/ArchiCAD via ODBC) <- manually-recorded data -> colour-coded 3D GUI; no ontology, no RDF/SPARQL
identity_mechanism: Database primary key 'E/P ID' per equipment/pipeline segment; correspondence to IFC GlobalId is never discussed or verified
validation_method: Single illustrative GUI screenshot walkthrough (Fig. 8); no query-correctness test of any kind; authors explicitly state empirical pilot testing is future work, not yet done
already_established: A concrete, named, schema-level BIM-component-to-maintenance-action linkage (Maintenance table: E/P ID + staff ID + date + reason + parts + cost) with genuine actor+timestamp fields; six-module decomposition of O&M information needs for a linear/underground asset type
remaining_gap: No ontology/formal semantic model at all (plain relational schema); Inspection concept named in a diagram but never instantiated as a table with fields; no timestamp shown for monitoring/sensor tables despite 'real-time' narrative claim; no model/version context; no validity scope; no query/CQ-based validation; no invalid/negative-link tests; framework itself not empirically validated by the authors' own admission
impact_on_paper2: Cannot claim novelty for 'BIM component should link to a maintenance record with an actor and date' at the concept level; can cite this paper's low formality ceiling (no ontology, no identity verification, no empirical validation) as exactly the maturity gap Paper 2 closes

citation: Matarneh, Elghaish, Rahimian, Dawood & Edwards (2022), Automation in Construction 143:104569
sensor_to_bim: IFC (Extended FM Handover View) -> bespoke C# STEP-line parser -> SQL Server COBie-schema DB (19 worksheets) <- SFG20 XML (preventive-maintenance standard) -> web GUI (admin/vendor roles) -> COBie-lizer (EPPlus) -> COBie .xlsx -> external CAFM/CMMS; no ontology, no RDF/SPARQL, no sensor data
bim_to_inspection: Parser follows IFC STEP internal line-number references (direct/inverse relationships); GlobalId/GUID persistence, duplicate handling, or export-verification is never explicitly discussed
already_established: Alpha testing (1 building, bug-finding) + beta testing (3 real projects, 12 FM-team members, 10-point Likert-scale usefulness/user-friendliness questionnaire, Table 2); purely a user-acceptance/usability study, no data-correctness check
impact_on_paper2: Automated IFC->COBie-schema->CAFM/CMMS pipeline validated on 3 real projects with 12 real users; genuine Type-level component-to-preventive-maintenance-task (Job) linkage; demonstrates by absence that the industry-standard COBie schema itself has no inspection concept and no condition-evidence concept
column25: No sensor/condition-evidence input of any kind (static as-built/handover data only); no inspection-record concept in the schema at all; maintenance linkage is Type-level, planned-only, with no execution status/closure; no provenance beyond coarse role-based access; no model/version context; no validity scope; no query/CQ-based correctness validation (only subjective usability survey); no invalid/negative-link tests
column26: Cannot claim novelty for automating BIM->FM-database transfer or for a component-to-maintenance-task linkage per se; differentiation rests entirely on sensor-derived evidence
column30: none of which this paper addresses

citation: Seiß, Zheng, Melzner, Wium & Seppänen (2025), Automation in Construction 177:106268
information_architecture: BIM (IFC2LBD) + schedule + BOQ (X83->CSV->R2RML) + inspection templates + inspection plan (planned+executed) -> RDF instance data -> OCQA ontology (core + catalog/regulation/contract + trade extensions) in Stardog -> SPARQL + Pellet-reasoner axiom-based inference -> prototype toolkit (Sparnatural + BIM viewer + schedule viewer)
identity_mechanism: Actual IFC GlobalId used directly as the component identifier (concrete example UUIDs 2EXbspDnzBfQetvaNkppij and 0owp2g3RTDcQ$khC3kGEsY, via dicp:hasObject); no duplicate-GUID handling, no export-verification, no per-GUID version binding discussed
validation_method: Multi-method: automated consistency check (Pellet + OOPS!); criteria-based evaluation; task-based evaluation with real project data (11 project-specific CQs, Table 4, concrete narrated answers); 2 focus groups with 11 domain experts total; no pre-registered expected-answer/pass-fail protocol with denominators reported
already_established: Direct binding to the actual IFC GlobalId (not a converter surrogate) demonstrated on real project data; rigorous multi-method CQ-driven ontology evaluation (closest existing precedent to Paper 2's own protocol); designed (unexercised) SSN/SOSA/SAREF sensor alignment and OPM/DiCon temporal-context alignment; genuine reverse/inverse-property SPARQL traversal and reasoner-based axiomatic classification; explicit requirement-provenance chain (BOQ item -> contract norm -> referenced tolerance norm)
remaining_gap: No maintenance/action-record concept at all (chain stops at the Inspection entity); no identity-verification/duplicate-GUID/export-verification layer around the GUID; no deliberate identity/link-integrity negative tests anywhere (clean gap even in the strongest paper reviewed); no pre-registered expected-answer set with explicit pass/fail and denominators; sensor-linkage and temporal/version-tracking capabilities are architecturally aligned but never empirically demonstrated; no validity-scope/applicability-set concept for evidence usability across contexts
impact_on_paper2: Single closest paper to Paper 2 and the strongest novelty threat on identity-binding and information-traceability fronts; cannot claim 'first CQ-based ontology evaluation for inspection/BIM linkage' or 'first use of actual IFC GUID for inspection binding'; defensible differentiation is a closed accountable Action_Status extension export-verified identity governance a pre-registered denominator-reporting expected-answer protocol and deliberate negative-fixture testing absent even here
